brock: United States ex rel. Brockenbrough v. TrueCore Behavioral Solutions, LLC, et al., No. 8:19-cv-02557 (U.S. District Court, M.D. Fla., Tampa Division), complaint filed Oct. 16, 2019
nyt02: The New York Times (Bloomberg News), Mar 9, 2002
dl: Digital Look, G4S share price page
djjcol: Florida Department of Juvenile Justice, Columbus Juvenile Residential Facility page (archived Apr 19, 2015)

paragraphs: G4S Youth Services was the American juvenile justice arm of the British security company G4S. From offices in Florida it ran state-contracted lockups and treatment programs for youths in Florida, Tennessee, Arkansas and Texas.{bw13,tm,wkrn} In 2002 some of the Florida facilities it later ran, including Avon Park Youth Academy, were run by Securicor New Century, a subsidiary of a British company; one of Securicor's three Florida sites had been the subject of a state report that guards abused teenagers and shackled one to a bed for 14 hours.{lvs,tm} For 15 years its facilities drew state sanctions and criminal investigations.{hc} In 2008 Florida declared it in default at Hastings Youth Academy after a youth's arm was broken in a restraint.{hc} In 2013 a riot broke out at Avon Park Youth Academy.{tm} In 2015 a grand jury called for Highlands Youth Academy to be closed.{fox13} Escapes followed at four of its Florida sites.{tb28,wptv,anj,wokv} In April 2017 G4S sold the business, which carried on as TrueCore Behavioral Solutions.{polk,bw20}

The Florida contracts go back to Securicor.{lvs} In 2002 Securicor New Century, of Richmond, Virginia, a subsidiary of the British firm Securicor, ran three Florida juvenile facilities, among them Avon Park Youth Academy in Polk County and Sago Palm Academy in western Palm Beach County.{lvs} It had taken over operations from Correctional Services Corp.{lvs} That August, when Nevada chose Securicor to run a youth prison, the losing bidder, Rite of Passage, pointed to a 2000 Florida Department of Juvenile Justice report that guards at Sago Palm had abused teenagers, shackled one to a bed for 14 hours and used a choke hold.{lvs} It also cited a 2001 state report that rated Avon Park's programs below average.{lvs} Securicor's chief executive, Gail Browne, said early problems had been corrected.{lvs} Group 4 Falck had bought the Wackenhut Corporation in 2002.{nyt02} In July 2004 Securicor merged with Group 4 Falck's security business to form Group 4 Securicor, later G4S.{dl} G4S Youth Services later said it had served more than 12,000 Florida youths since 2002.{tb28}

The division grew mainly through Florida Department of Juvenile Justice contracts.{tm} By August 2013 it ran 16 state facilities: 13 in Florida, two in Tennessee and one in Arkansas.{tm} The Arkansas site was the state's Juvenile Assessment and Treatment Center near Alexander, which it ran from 2007.{ark} In Nashville it ran the G4S Academy for Young Men, also called Stones River Academy, a program for 24 boys committed to the Tennessee Department of Children's Services.{wkrn} In March 2013 Brown County, Texas, agreed to lease part of its juvenile justice building in Brownwood to the company.{bw13} In 2015 Florida's Department of Juvenile Justice listed G4S Youth Services as the provider of the Columbus Juvenile Residential Facility in Tampa, later Columbus Youth Academy.{djjcol}

Its record in Florida went bad early.{hc} After a February 2008 incident, a Hastings Youth Academy employee, Kutanna Woods, was fired for using unnecessary force on a youth, who suffered a broken shoulder.{hc} His lawyer said surveillance video showed her twisting his arm behind his back until it broke after he refused to sweep a floor.{hc} The department's inspector general found that staff used unnecessary force, but the sheriff declined to file charges.{hc} In March 2008 the department declared G4S in default of its Hastings contract, citing serious incidents, inappropriate staff-youth relationships and no effective behavior management system.{hc} It lifted the notice that July, saying the company had substantially complied.{hc}

The problems continued for years.{tm} In August 2013, 21 staff were on shift for 144 youths when a riot broke out at Avon Park Youth Academy, and 64 youths were sent to the Polk County Jail.{tm} In July 2015 a Polk County grand jury said Highlands Youth Academy, which G4S ran under a five-year, $40 million state contract, should be closed.{fox13} In early 2016 a youth escaped from Falkenburg Academy in Tampa, and no one called 911 for more than 13 hours; four staff members were suspended.{tb28} That May six youths escaped from the Okeechobee Youth Development Center.{wptv} In June 2017 the state froze admissions at Hastings after its third escape in three months, citing critical failures in how the company supervised youths.{anj} Youths escaped from Jacksonville Youth Academy that month too.{wokv} In August 2017 three former Highlands administrators were arrested.{polk} The sheriff said G4S staff there had routinely covered up fights, uses of force, contraband and escapes.{polk}

By then G4S was leaving the business.{ark} In May 2016 the division's president, Jim Hill, and Brian Neupaver, who ran its operations, left for a rival, Youth Opportunity Investments, and G4S sued both men and the new company in Florida.{ark} That July Rite of Passage won the $34.1 million Arkansas contract G4S had held since 2007.{ark} On April 1, 2017, G4S sold its American youth business to BHSB Holdings for $56.5 million, and it was renamed TrueCore Behavioral Solutions.{polk,wkrn,bw20} On October 16, 2019, TrueCore's former chief operating officer, Rodney Brockenbrough, filed a sealed whistleblower complaint in federal court in Tampa against TrueCore and its owners that also named G4S US, G4S Youth Services, LLC and G4S Secure Solutions.{brock} It alleged that a nonprofit, the Henry & Rilla White Youth Foundation, posed as the owner of 19 for-profit G4S and TrueCore youth facilities so they could collect National School Lunch Program money that only nonprofits may receive.{brock} TrueCore left Texas in June 2020 and handed The Oaks in Brownwood to Rite of Passage.{bw20}
